facts.text: EN 14363 is the European rail standard for approving how a vehicle runs on track; DynoTRAIN is the research project that built its simulation-validation method.
facts.quote: EN 14363 is the European rail standard for approving how a vehicle runs on track

facts.text: EN 14363 is the only standard identified in the booklet that formally allows a validated simulation to extend acceptance to new conditions and modified vehicles.
facts.quote: it is the one standard in the booklet that formally lets a validated simulation extend acceptance to new conditions and modified vehicles

facts.text: Approval of a new train in Europe normally involves measuring running behavior—stability, forces on the rail and ride—on real track.
facts.quote: When a new train is approved in Europe, its running behavior (stability, forces on the rail, ride) is normally measured on real track.

facts.text: EN 14363:2016+A2:2022 adds two informative annexes: Annex T on simulating on-track tests and Annex U on extending acceptance.
facts.quote: EN 14363:2016+A2:2022 adds two informative annexes: Annex T on simulating on-track tests and Annex U on extending acceptance.

facts.text: Under the EN 14363 approach, running tests validate the vehicle model; the validated model may then extend tested conditions, assess a modified vehicle or compare against an approved reference vehicle.
facts.quote: Running tests validate the vehicle model; the validated model may then extend the range of tested conditions, assess a modified vehicle, or compare against an approved reference vehicle.

facts.text: The European Union Agency for Railways publishes guidance on using validated simulation to extend rail-vehicle acceptance.
facts.quote: The European Union Agency for Railways publishes guidance on doing this

facts.text: The DynoTRAIN project built the rail simulation-validation method, with results published from 2014 to 2015.
facts.quote: The DynoTRAIN project (results published 2014 to 2015) built the method.

facts.text: DynoTRAIN compared several vehicle models, several software tools and measurements from multiple vehicles and countries, using more than 1,000 simulations.
facts.quote: It compared several vehicle models, several software tools and measurements from multiple vehicles and countries, with more than 1,000 simulations.

facts.text: DynoTRAIN found that checking large numbers of plots by engineering judgment does not scale, prompting development of objective validation metrics.
facts.quote: Its key finding was that checking large numbers of plots by engineering judgment does not scale, so objective validation metrics were developed.

facts.text: The validation practice resulting from DynoTRAIN judges agreement using at least 24 simulation-versus-measurement comparisons per quantity from at least 12 track sections, with validation limits on the means and standard deviations across the comparison set.
facts.quote: at least 24 simulation-versus-measurement comparisons per quantity from at least 12 track sections, with validation limits on the means and standard deviations across the set

facts.text: The booklet rates rail practice as the strongest precedent for transferring acceptance across vehicle families and reducing physical tests.
facts.quote: The booklet rates rail as the strongest precedent for family transfer and test reduction

facts.text: Wheel-rail dynamics are far more deterministic than perception in dust, rain, glare or snow, so the rail acceptance-transfer mechanism transfers to the off-road validation program, not the physics.
facts.quote: wheel-rail dynamics are far more deterministic than perception in dust, rain, glare or snow, so the mechanism transfers, not the physics.

facts.text: No percentage of physical tests actually removed through the rail simulation-validation practice was published.
facts.quote: No percentage of physical tests actually removed was published
